A. Mastermix preparation and PCR set up Pipet 4.95µl PCR grade water, 12.5µl 2X Buffer-Qiagen Multiplex PCR Kit (catalogue number 206143) and 1uM of each primer per reaction in the labeled microcentrifuge PCR master mix tube (multiply the volumes by the number of reactions). Vortex and spin briefly the tube with the prepared PCR master mix. Pipet 22.5µl PCR master mix in each labelled 96-Well Plate/strip well. Add 2.5µl PCR grade water to the well labeled as negative control. Cover the wells containing the PCR master mix with 8-cap strips and take the 96-Well Plate to another biosafety cabinet, if possible, in another room. Add 2.5µl of each DNA sample and S. agalactiae serotype DNA controls to the respective wells. Close the filled wells and press the caps tightly. Enter the amplification parameters on the thermal cycler as follows: 6. Check the sample volume and review the parameters on the thermo cycler screen and start the run.

2. Agarose gel preparation On a precision scale, weigh 1.6g Nusieve® agarose (catalogue number 50090). Mix the weighed agarose with 80ml room temperature 1X TAE buffer (2% gel final concentration). Heat in microwave for 90 seconds. Using thermoresistant gloves, carefully mix the solution, checking against the light to see if the agarose is completely dissolved, adding more time in the microwave as needed. Let the agarose solution cool down to 50°C (about 5 minutes), add 5µl (0.5µg/µl) of EtBr. Pour the gel on a casting tray with a 24 wells comb and wait until it solidifies. If not using the gel in the same day, cover the gel with 1X TAE buffer and put it in the refrigerator until ready to use.

1. In a BSC, prepare the initial bacteria suspension. Depending on the organism being extracted, use the following amounts: For Streptococcus agalactiae , using a 1µl loop, transfer 2-3 colonies of overnight blood agar plate growth to a labeled microcentrifuge tube containing 300µl of 0.85% NaCl and vortex. 2. Heat the suspension at 70⁰C for 15 minutes, use cap holder to secure the lid. 3. Spin microcentrifuge tube for 2 minutes in centrifuge at 10,000 rpm and remove supernatant. 4. Re-suspend the pellet in 50µl TE buffer, add 12µl mutanolysin (solution 2500U/ml) and 8µl of hyaluronidase (solution 30mg/ml) and vortex. The mutanolysin solution is prepared by dissolving 10,000 units of mutanolysin (Sigma #M9901) into 4ml of PCR water (2500unit/ml stock solution); stored in aliquots of 500µl at -20⁰C. The hyaluronidase solution is prepared by dissolving 100mg hyaluronidase (Sigma #H3506) into 3.3ml PCR water (30mg/ml stock solution); stored in 500µl aliquots at -20⁰C. 5. Heat the suspension in water bath at 37⁰C for 30 minutes to overnight. 6. Heat the suspension to inactivate for 10 minutes in 100⁰C heat block, use cap holder to secure the lid. 7. Spin the tube for 4 minutes in centrifuge, identify the tube with the cryogenic label and use the DNA template in the supernatant. 8. Proceed immediately with PCR reaction or store lysates at -20⁰C until use. steps.title: Thaw and Prepare Specimens
steps.instruction: Thaw vaginal/rectal (V/R)‑STGG specimens at room temperature (25 °C), vortex 10–20 s, then re‑freeze the STGG as soon as possible and keep it on ice; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Enrich in LIM Broth
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µl of the V/R‑STGG to 5 ml LIM broth (BD‑BBL cat# 296266) containing 1 ml rabbit serum (Gibco cat# 16120099), vortex, and incubate 5 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Plate on CHROMID Strepto B
steps.instruction: Vortex the enriched LIM broth, inoculate one loop (≈10 µl) onto CHROMID® Strepto B agar (BioMérieux cat# 419751) and incubate 18–24 h at 37 °C in a CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Examine and Subculture Colonies
steps.instruction: After 24 h, examine CHROMID® Strepto B for pale‑pink to red colonies typical of GBS; pick a single suspected colony, streak onto a fresh blood agar plate (BAP) and incubate 18–24 h at 37 °C in CO₂.

steps.title: Perform Identification Tests
steps.instruction: Subject the subcultured isolate to Gram stain, CAMP test, and latex agglutination (PathDx Strep B latex – R62031).

substeps.instruction: Gram stain according to routine protocol.
CAMP test as described in step 6.
Latex agglutination as described in step 7.

steps.title: Freeze Confirmed Isolates
steps.instruction: If identification is confirmed, freeze the fresh 24‑h culture in STGG or sheep blood and store at –70 °C for later serotyping or antimicrobial testing.

steps.title: Conduct CAMP Test
steps.instruction: Streak the suspected GBS isolate and Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 onto a BAP at a 90° angle, incubate 18–24 h at 37 °C with CO₂, and read a positive result as a triangular zone of enhanced β‑hemolysis between the two streaks.

steps.title: Perform Latex Agglutination
steps.instruction: Clean and label a slide, place a drop of 0.85 % saline, add a heavy loop of fresh BAP growth, mix to a milky suspension, add one drop of PathDx Strep B latex (flask shaken beforehand), and rock the slide for 1 min; agglutination indicates a positive result.

steps.title: Prepare Gel for PCR Products
steps.instruction: Remove the comb, place the agarose gel in the electrophoresis unit, and fill the unit with refrigerated 1× TAE buffer until the gel is completely covered.

steps.title: Load Samples and Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load 15 µl of 50‑bp ladder (catalogue 70538‑3) into the first and last wells; mix each 10 µl amplified DNA with 1 µl gel‑loading dye and load into the remaining wells according to the template; run at 100 V for 90 min.

steps.title: Capture Gel Image and Analyze Bands
steps.instruction: After electrophoresis, turn off the unit, remove the gel, place it on a UV transilluminator, photograph, and compare band patterns to S. agalactiae serotype controls; assign a serotype only when sample band sizes exactly match the control sizes (note possible non‑specific bands).

steps.title: Interpret Serotype PCR Results
steps.instruction: Confirm that each sample shows the 688 bp capsular gene (cps I) band common to all serotypes; determine the serotype by the presence of the serotype‑specific band sizes listed in the assay table.

steps.title: Prepare Inoculum for MIC Testing
steps.instruction: From a pure overnight BAP culture, transfer several colonies into 5 ml saline or Mueller‑Hinton broth, vortex, adjust turbidity to 0.5 McFarland (≈1.5 × 10⁸ CFU/ml) using a 0.5 McFarland standard or densitometer, and use the suspension within 15 min.

steps.title: Inoculate MIC Panel and Incubate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of the adjusted suspension to Mueller‑Hinton broth with lysed horse blood, mix gently, dispense into a sterile reservoir, open the S. agalactiae MIC panel, label with isolate ID, add 100 µl of inoculated broth to each well using a multichannel pipette, seal the panel with a plate seal, and incubate at ambient air 35–37 °C for 20–24 h.

steps.title: Read and Record MIC Endpoints
steps.instruction: After incubation, read the panel with a parabolic magnifying mirror and light; record the first well showing no visible growth (100 % inhibition) as the MIC endpoint and interpret results according to the latest CLSI M100‑S22 guidelines.
